description: A lamp hangs low on its hooked flex and lays a hot apricot pool across the trodden straw, while cold slate blue comes in flat through the open doorway behind it.
A hurricane lantern set down on a bale throws a warm amber spread across the pen boards and the ewe's broad back, the rest of the shed a plain cool grey.
A low copper sun under a bruise-purple hail cloud, the wet grass lit acid green against it and every breath showing in the cold still air.
Flat pearl-grey overcast right across the whole sky, every blade of new grass gone deep saturated green underneath, the air cold and completely motionless.
Hard blue pre-dawn light, cold and completely even, every surface the same pale blue-grey and the cold air utterly still with nothing moving in it.
A lamp hangs in plain sight above the pen, its hot apricot circle landing on the straw and the rim of the crate, while the planked walls behind stay a deep cool blue-grey.
Sun breaking through right as a hail shower goes over, the air full of bright white grains and the wet grass lit a hard saturated green beneath a pale gold sky.
Thin silver drizzle falling straight down through still air, the stone wall gone near-black with wet and every green surface deep and heavy with it.
The open doorway lets in a flat band of cold lilac morning across the plank walkway; a lamp hangs above the pen and keeps the straw apricot-warm on one side.
A cold violet dusk with the new grass reading almost turquoise under it, the stone wall a deep charcoal and the sky still holding a thin strip of pale gold at the horizon.
Full hard midday sun, the air perfectly still and dry, every surface bleached to a warm cream-white except the new grass which holds a bright acid green.
Low copper sunlight coming straight in along the length of the shed from the open end, laying a warm orange-gold band across the whitewashed wall and the top of the hurdle rails.
A wind pushing the new grass all one way, the blades lit bright yellow-green on top and dark bottle-green underneath, the sky above a deep saturated cobalt.
Steam lifting off the wet backs of ewes in cold still air, the light a pale silver-white from high thin cloud and every fleece gone a deep cream-ivory under it.
A lamp hangs on its flex above two pens and its apricot pool lands on a lamb's damp curls and across the ewe's flank, while the far end of the shed holds a flat pewter cool.
A bruise-purple squall moving in from the left, the near field still in hard gold sun and the wet grass lit a fierce acid green against the dark sky behind it.
A cold clear dawn, the sky a sharp rose-pink above a band of pale gold at the horizon, the air showing every breath and completely windless.
Chaff and straw dust up in a wide hot-apricot spread from the lamp hanging above the bale, the plank walkway warm ochre beneath and the doorway behind it a cool grey-blue.
A flat overcast with a soft diffuse pink in it at the east, the grass a deep saturated green and the dry-stone wall a pale cool grey all along its length.
Still, cold air with absolutely nothing moving in it, the light a flat even silver from a high white sky and every surface carrying the same cool blue-grey tone.
A lamp hangs in plain sight on a bent nail above the pen; its warm amber landing on the rim of the wooden box and across the ewe's back while the boarded wall behind stays a plain cool slate.
Hail grains bouncing hard off the field gate and the stone wall, the sky above a yellow-grey, the wet grass between the bouncing grains a fierce dark green.
A butter-yellow low sun in a clear pale-blue sky, the air cold, dry and dead still, every shadow a sharp clean edge and the cold pulling every breath visible.
The gap between two boards lets a flat bright band of gold morning light across a lamb's back and the straw beside it; the rest of the pen stays a deep blue-grey cool.
Fine drizzle in a wind, the grass flattened and bright dark green, the stone wall running with water and gone almost black, the sky a pale smeared silver.
The one translucent sheet set into the tin roof drops a broad cool white rectangle onto the straw below it, and the far end of the shed holds a deep warm brown.
The shed door stands wide and is the whole light in the room, a broad flat band of cold blue laid across the straw inside it, the pens beyond it a warm chestnut.
A hand torch left lying on the top rail throws a hard white circle across the straw and one lambs flank, the boarded wall behind it a plain deep indigo.
Two colours meet down the length of the shed: cold pewter coming in at the open end, hot amber on the straw at the near pens, chaff drifting between them.
